title: JavaScript beginner module (≈ 8–10 lessons + graded exercises)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The JavaScript module is the second language in the curriculum and the proof that the language-agnostic content model works. Adding it must require only a JS runner adapter + original JS content, with no schema changes. The module must cover the same conceptual ground as the Python module (variables, types, control flow, functions) but using JavaScript idioms.
objective: Author a complete JavaScript beginner module of approximately 8–10 lessons (variables/let/const, types/coercion, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, objects, and basic error handling) — each with original prose, at least one runnable example, and at least one graded exercise — demonstrating the language-agnostic model.
acceptanceCriteria: At least 8 lessons are delivered covering JavaScript beginner fundamentals: variables (let/const/var distinction), types and coercion, operators, conditionals, loops, functions, arrays, and objects.
Every lesson has at least 1 runnable example and at least 1 graded exercise with solutionVerified:true (CI-set using the JS adapter) and starter code that does NOT pass the tests.
All prose is original; at least 2 authoritative cited sources per lesson (ECMAScript spec or MDN cited but not copied — MDN is CC-BY-SA and must be cited, not copied into CC-BY prose).
Each lesson is schema-valid; no new schema fields or contract changes were required to add JavaScript.
Technical correctness and pedagogy review by non-authors for all lessons.
Examples are neutral/inclusive; prerequisites honestly stated.
output: A set of merged lesson documents (with exercise files) for the JavaScript beginner module, each schema-valid, correctness-verified via the JS adapter, and technically + pedagogically reviewed.
